For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law
**Status of Seller material:** Other side's draft – reviewed critically below. The Seller's covering note describes the package as "fair and balanced"; it is not. Read together, the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter are an attempt to (a) collapse every protection into one capped, time-limited regime, (b) shift known, quantified risks onto the Buyer via general disclosure and a knowledge exclusion, and (c) defer the two most important pre-completion deliverables (Bluefen consent and Riverlark release) to "after Completion".

Several items the Seller labels as "settled", "adequate" or "not expected to be material" are, on the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, unresolved and quantifiable. The Disclosure Letter is actually helpful to us: it concedes a number of gaps (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, bonuses not in funds flow, Ironquay unpaid, incident unresolved). We should use those concessions.

---

## Part A – Material issues (in order of priority)

### 1. Fundamental / title warranties folded into the general cap and 18-month window — reject

**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) and 18-month limit as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".

**Why this matters:** If title to the shares fails, we have paid AUD 24m and may own nothing (or less than 100%). A cap of AUD 4.8m on that outcome is commercially indefensible and well outside market. Note also Disclosure Letter [10]: the Seller relies solely on the share register at DD-012 and expressly says this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification". That is a signal, not comfort.

**Push back:**
- Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency, share capital/no other securities) capped at 100% of the price, with a limitation period of 6 years (or the statutory limitation period, whichever is longer) from Completion.
- Fundamental warranties and specific indemnities carved out of de minimis and basket.
- Independent title verification: ASIC company search, share register inspection, review of constitution and any shareholder agreements, confirmation of no options/convertibles/ESOP, and a warranty that the register is complete and accurate. Do not accept DD-012 as the sole evidence.

### 2. "All limitations apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5) — reject

**Seller position:** Caps, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to every Claim unless expressly stated otherwise; tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime".

**Why this matters:** This single drafting choice sweeps in title, tax, specific indemnities, and leakage claims. Combined with issue 1, the Seller's maximum exposure for anything becomes AUD 4.8m with an 18-month fuse. It also means a Tax Warranty Claim would expire long before the ATO's review period, and an indemnity for a known Ironquay or data incident problem would be subject to de minimis/basket thresholds that it was never intended to carry.

**Push back:**
- Reverse the default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
- Separate regime for: Fundamental Warranties; Tax Warranties and Tax Indemnity (cap 100%, period = later of 7 years / expiry of ATO amendment period plus 60 days); Specific Indemnities (uncapped or separately capped, no de minimis/basket, 6 years); Leakage/debt-free cash-free adjustments (dollar-for-dollar, no thresholds).
- Nothing in cl 12 or 20.5 to limit liability for fraud, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct — confirm this carve-out is express.
- Exclusive-remedy clause must not exclude claims under the specific indemnities, the price adjustment mechanics, or injunctive relief for restraints/confidentiality.
- Non-reliance (cl 20.5) must not be drafted to exclude liability under the Australian Consumer Law for misleading or deceptive conduct where that is not permitted, and must not operate as a disclosure of matters not actually disclosed.

### 3. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3) + general data room disclosure (Sch 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2]) — reject in current form

**Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". Disclosure Letter discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".

**Why this matters:** Taken together these clauses mean the Buyer carries every risk that any adviser *could* have found anywhere, regardless of whether it was actually understood or whether it was fairly disclosed. "Discoverable from public records" is open-ended (ASIC, PPSR, court lists, IP Australia, land titles). "Advisers' knowledge" imputes to the Buyer the knowledge of every lawyer, accountant and consultant. This converts warranties from risk allocation into a nullity.

**Push back:**
- Delete cl 8.3 entirely, or confine it to actual knowledge of a named short list of deal team individuals, excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and excluding advisers.
- Disclosure standard: only matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter". General disclosure of the data room is acceptable only on that standard, and only against the specific warranties to which a document is reasonably referable.
- Delete disclosure of "publicly searchable corporate records" (or limit to ASIC company extract and PPSR search of the Company as at a fixed date, with copies in the data room).
- Data room to be frozen and an indexed copy delivered on USB/escrow at signing; data room cut-off (22 Sept 2026) should be at least 2 Business Days before signing, with no additions after cut-off.
- Importantly: general disclosure must not disclose against the specific indemnities or the Fundamental Warranties. The Seller's attempt to generally disclose DD-002 to DD-012 is aimed squarely at every known problem listed below.

### 4. Bluefen change-of-control consent (cl 3/6.3) — condition precedent, not "reasonable endeavours"

**Seller position:** Consent "is addressed"; Seller will use reasonable endeavours and will "treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".

**Disclosure Letter [2]:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue); cl 11.2 requires consent and cl 11.3 attaches conditions; **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.

**Why this matters:** 30% of revenue is at risk if Bluefen terminates on change of control. The Seller's covering note says "addressed"; its own Disclosure Letter says not obtained. "Reasonable endeavours" is the lowest endeavours standard. "Treat as satisfied on delivery of written consent" is drafted so that a conditional or qualified consent letter could tick the box without the 11.3 conditions being met.

**Push back:**
- Hard condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or consent on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), in a form approved by the Buyer, together with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived by Bluefen, and no notice of termination/repricing. Condition for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by the Buyer.
- Seller obligation: "all reasonable endeavours" / "best endeavours" including Buyer participation in discussions with Bluefen.
- Warranty that Bluefen has not indicated an intention to terminate, reduce volume or reprice; specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates within 12 months of Completion in connection with the change of control. Consider a revenue-linked deferred consideration component if the Seller resists.

### 5. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7) — must be discharged at Completion, not "following Completion"

**Seller position:** AUD 3.2m facility "addressed by a release to be provided following Completion".

**Disclosure Letter [3]:** facility not repaid; change-of-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2; no discharge of security in data room.

**Why this matters:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If we complete with AUD 3.2m of bank debt still on the Company's balance sheet and a change-of-control trigger in cl 8.1, (a) the bank can call the facility on Completion, (b) its security remains over the Company's assets (and possibly the shares), and (c) we have overpaid by AUD 3.2m unless the price mechanics deduct it. A post-Completion release leaves us with no leverage.

**Push back:**
- Completion deliverable: payout letter from Riverlark, executed deed of release/discharge of all security (and PPSR discharge of registrations within 5 Business Days), and release of any guarantees. Funds flow to direct the repayment amount from the purchase price to Riverlark at Completion.
- Riverlark's pre-consent (or waiver of cl 8.1) to be obtained before Completion if the facility is not being fully repaid at Completion for any reason.
- Confirm the funds flow treats the full payout figure (including break costs and accrued interest to Completion) as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free adjustment.
- PPSR search of the Company immediately before Completion to confirm no other registrations.

### 6. DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420,000) — not in the funds flow

**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised in the funds flow."

**Disclosure Letter [5]:** AUD 420k of Completion bonuses, conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; disclosure silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.

**Why this matters:** These bonuses are triggered by the transaction and are payable by the Company after Completion to employees who remain. Unless they are deducted from the price as Transaction Costs/Debt (plus on-costs: superannuation guarantee at the current rate, NSW payroll tax, any leave accruals), the Buyer funds AUD 420k+ of the Seller's deal cost. "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the Seller actually pays them.

**Push back:**
- Treat as Debt / Transaction Bonuses in the completion adjustment, grossed up for employer on-costs (estimate on-costs at roughly 15–20%, so ~AUD 480–500k total), or require the Seller to pay them through payroll at or before Completion with evidence.
- Itemise in the funds flow.
- Warranty that no other transaction-related payments, retention bonuses, accelerated vesting or change-of-control entitlements exist beyond DD-005.
- Confirm whether the "continued-employment" condition creates a post-Completion payment obligation for the Company and, if so, that the Seller funds it via escrow.

### 7. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) — indemnity is too narrow; this is a title-to-IP problem

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment "and is considered adequate".

**Disclosure Letter [4]:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment on file.

**Why this matters:** The exposure is not AUD 180,000. On the contract's own terms, until payment clears the Company **does not own** the SOW3 deliverables. If those materials are embedded in the Paperbark product, the Company is using IP it does not own, with licence, infringement and customer-contract consequences. An indemnity for the "payment" does not cure a title defect.

**Push back:**
- Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees (bank confirmation, not just an internal ledger), Ironquay written acknowledgment of payment, and an executed confirmatory deed of assignment of all Project Materials (SOW1–3, not just SOW3) with moral rights consents from Ironquay's personnel.
- Specific indemnity covering all loss arising from any failure of title to Ironquay-developed materials, any Ironquay claim, and the cost of re-development or licensing — uncapped or capped at the full price, no thresholds, 6 years.
- Diligence: map which Ironquay deliverables are in production code. Ask whether SOW1 and SOW2 had similar conditional-transfer language.
- The AUD 180,000 itself should be paid pre-Completion by the Seller or deducted as Debt.

### 8. DD-006 data export / privacy incident — not "preliminary and immaterial"

**Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."

**Disclosure Letter [6]:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation "preliminary"; no loss stated.

**Why this matters:** The 30-day assessment window under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme is likely already running from the point the Company became aware of the incident. If this is an eligible data breach, notification to the OAIC and affected individuals is mandatory, and the affected individuals are likely customer-side contacts — potentially including Bluefen personnel. Civil penalties for serious/repeated interferences with privacy are substantial following the 2022 amendments. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an opinion; its Disclosure Letter [1.4] expressly refuses to admit that any notification is required. We cannot accept the Seller's characterisation and the uncertainty is itself the problem.

**Push back:**
- Pre-signing: demand the incident log, the date of awareness, link-access logs (whether the link was clicked/downloaded), the identity of the recipient domain, steps taken to revoke the link, and any legal advice obtained (privileged summary at minimum). Require the assessment to be completed before Completion.
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from DD-006 (regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, customer claims, contract termination), outside the cap and thresholds.
- Warranty that there have been no other data incidents, and that the Company's privacy practices comply with the Privacy Act and the APPs.
- Condition or covenant that the Company makes any required OAIC/individual notifications before Completion, with Buyer approval of the form.
- Cross-check with Bluefen (issue 4): if Bluefen contacts are in the export and Bluefen's contract has a security/incident notification clause, non-notification may itself be a breach that undermines the consent process.

### 9. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000) — Seller is unable to say whether they are ordinary course

**Seller position:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."

**Disclosure Letter [8]:** three related renewals of AUD 110k each; "read together for timing/scope"; disclosure **does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course**.

**Why this matters:** The Seller Update asserts ordinary course; the Disclosure Letter refuses to. Three identical AUD 110k contracts described as "related" with an instruction to read them together suggests either a single AUD 330k commitment split to stay under approval thresholds, or a bundled arrangement with cross-termination. Either way the Seller is pre-emptively disclosing against the ordinary-course and material-contracts warranties.

**Push back:**
- Obtain DD-008 and DD-011 in full; confirm counterparty, term, termination rights, auto-renewal dates, and whether any renewal was signed after the locked-box/accounts date.
- If committed after the accounts date and not reflected in working capital, treat as leakage or a working capital adjustment.
- Require Seller to either warrant that the renewals are terminable without penalty on ≤90 days' notice or to carve them into the price.
- Add a specific warranty that there are no other split or related commitments.

### 10. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) — confirm, don't accept the Seller's reading

Disclosure Letter [7] and [9] are framed as "the provision does not say consent is required". That is the Seller's interpretation, unsupported by legal analysis, and [1.4] disclaims any admission on whether notices or consents are required.

**Push back:**
- Lease: review DD-007 ourselves. Even if only a notification obligation applies, require the notification to be given pre-Completion in agreed form and a warranty that the landlord has not asserted a consent right. Check for deemed-assignment provisions on change in control of the tenant.
- Mossvale: review DD-009's assignment restriction for change-of-control or "deemed assignment" language. If genuinely silent, warranty that no consent is required and no notice of termination has been received; if ambiguous, obtain Mossvale comfort letter pre-Completion.

### 11. General liability regime (cl 12.1–12.3) — negotiable but not as proposed

- **Cap 20% (AUD 4.8m):** Low but within the broader market range for a private sale of this size. Acceptable only if issues 1, 2 and 7–8 are carved out. If the Seller insists on an all-in cap, counter at 50% and hold. Given the volume of known issues, consider a warranty and indemnity insurance quote — the Seller's position becomes more acceptable if W&I sits above a reduced Seller cap, but W&I will exclude known issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006), which reinforces the need for specific indemnities.
- **De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k (~1%):** De minimis is on the high side; propose AUD 10,000. Basket at 1% is broadly market as a "tipping" basket (first dollar recoverable once exceeded); the Seller's draft is a **deductible** (only the excess). Push for tipping basket. Neither threshold to apply to Fundamental, Tax, or Specific Indemnity claims.
- **18 months:** Acceptable for general warranties only if it is a notification period plus a reasonable time to commence proceedings (e.g. 6–9 months after notice), and provided that Tax (7 years) and Fundamental (6 years) run separately.
- Confirm the usual Buyer-side carve-outs are present: fraud, wilful default, Seller's knowledge; and that any "Seller's knowledge" qualifiers on warranties are expressly defined (actual knowledge of named individuals after due enquiry).

### 12. Disclosure Letter drafting points

- [1.4] "Nothing in this letter admits … that any consent, payment, notice … is legally required" — this is the Seller trying to disclose facts without disclosing their legal consequence. Insert: disclosures are made against specific warranties only, must be fair, and do not operate as disclosure against the specific indemnities or the Fundamental Warranties.
- [11] "No expected conclusion or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate…" — the Seller is attempting to shift the burden of characterising its own disclosures onto us. Reject the implication that the Buyer is deemed to have analysed and accepted every data room item.
- Require specific disclosures to be cross-referenced to warranty numbers in Schedule 7.
- Bring-down: Disclosure Letter to be updated at Completion only for matters arising after signing, with a Buyer termination right if new disclosures are material, and no updated disclosure to cure a warranty breach for claims purposes.

### 13. Tax and IP warranties — "settled" is premature

The Seller treats tax and IP as "settled under the general regime". They are not, for the reasons in issue 2. Separately:
- Tax: obtain a full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (standard in Australian SPAs), covering GST, income tax, payroll tax, super guarantee charge (relevant to DD-005), and any tax on the DD-005 bonuses. Confirm tax consolidation status and exit obligations if Paperbark is in the Harbourglass consolidated group (tax sharing/funding agreement, clear exit).
- IP: warranties as to ownership of all IP used in the business, no third-party claims, employee/contractor assignments in place, open-source compliance. Ironquay (issue 7) shows the contractor-assignment chain is not clean; ask for the assignment status of every developer/contractor.

---

## Part B – Items where the Seller's note and its Disclosure Letter contradict each other

| Topic | Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen consent | "addressed" | not obtained; 11.3 conditions not evidenced |
| Riverlark | "addressed by release following Completion" | not repaid; no discharge in data room |
| Ironquay | indemnity "adequate" | AUD 180k open; no receipt; no assignment |
| Bonuses | "matter for the Seller" | AUD 420k not in funds flow; on-costs unknown |
| Incident | "not expected to be material" | scope, access, and notification all unknown |
| Sandbar | "ordinary course" | Seller cannot say whether ordinary course |
| Title | "evidenced by register" | Buyer verification not done |

Use these in the mark-up covering letter: the Seller cannot simultaneously characterise matters as resolved for SPA purposes and reserve on them for disclosure purposes.

---

## Part C – Summary of recommendations

**Must have (deal-critical):**
1. Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital) at 100% cap, 6-year period, outside thresholds; independent title verification.
2. Reverse the "all limitations apply to all Claims" default; separate regimes for Fundamental, Tax, Specific Indemnities and price adjustments; fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out.
3. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion (or confine to actual knowledge of named individuals, no advisers, no "discoverable" standard).
4. Bluefen: unconditional consent with cl 11.3 conditions satisfied as a Buyer-only-waivable condition precedent; consider revenue-linked protection.
5. Riverlark: payout and executed release of security as Completion deliverables; funded from the price at Completion; PPSR discharge.
6. DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs deducted from price or paid pre-Completion with evidence; itemised in funds flow.
7. Ironquay: cleared payment, confirmatory assignment and moral rights consents as Completion deliverables; uncapped specific indemnity for IP title failure.
8. DD-006: full incident information pre-signing; assessment completed and any notifications made pre-Completion; uncapped specific indemnity.

**Should have:**
9. Fair-disclosure standard; data room frozen and escrowed; delete "publicly searchable records"; general disclosure not to apply to indemnities or Fundamental Warranties.
10. Tipping (not deductible) basket; de minimis AUD 10k; thresholds not applicable to Fundamental/Tax/Indemnity claims; 18 months with claim-commencement tail; Tax 7 years.
11. Standard pre-Completion tax indemnity; confirm tax consolidation exit.
12. Sandbar: full contracts, termination analysis, leakage/working capital treatment if post-accounts date.
13. Lease and Mossvale: our own review; pre-Completion notice/comfort letters; warranties that no consent is required.

**Process:**
14. Obtain a W&I quote now so we know what the market will cover above the Seller cap; it will not cover items 4–8, which is why those need specific indemnities.
15. Consider an escrow/retention (e.g. AUD 2.4m, 10%) for 18–24 months given the number of known open items, or a price chip to the extent the Seller refuses specific indemnities.
16. Do not sign while the Disclosure Letter [11] reservation and [1.4] no-admission language stand in their current form.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up of the SPA and a response letter to Harbourglass counsel once you confirm the priority ordering and your appetite on cap and escrow.
